title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts"

Fa Fa [1999] No. 28

To all local people's courts at various levels throughout the country, military courts at all levels, railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, maritime courts, and courts at all levels of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The "Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts" is hereby issued for your earnest implementation. Please promptly report any issues encountered during implementation to this Court.

Attachment: Explanation of the "Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts"

October 20, 1999

Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts

The Fifteenth National Congress of the Communist Party of China established the basic strategy of governing the country according to law and clearly set forth the task of advancing judicial reform. The Second Session of the Ninth National People's Congress incorporated this basic strategy of governing the country according to law into the Constitution. The reform of the people's courts is an important component of China's judicial reform and must be advanced actively and steadily so that the people's courts can play an essential and significant role in the historical process of governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law.

I. Seize the Opportunity to Advance the Reform of the People's Courts

1. Reform of the people's courts is imperative. With the gradual establishment of the socialist market economy system, China's economic system reform, democracy and legal system construction, and socialist cultural and ethical progress have achieved remarkable results. At the same time, due to changes in social relations, adjustments in the pattern of interests, and intertwined social contradictions, the trial work of the people's courts faces an unprecedented complex situation, and the management system and trial working mechanism of the people's courts have encountered severe challenges.

-- Local protectionism in judicial activities has spread, seriously endangering the unity and authority of China's socialist legal system;

-- The current judge management system makes it difficult for the overall quality of judges to meet the professional requirements of trial work and to resist the erosion of decadent ideas such as money worship, hedonism, and privilege mentality. The people have strong complaints about the corruption of a few judicial personnel and unfair judgments, directly damaging the prestige of the Party and the state;

-- The administrative management model of trial work does not suit the characteristics and laws of trial work, severely affecting the full play of the functions of the people's courts;

-- The people's courts, especially basic-level people's courts, face financial difficulties, outdated equipment, and inadequate material support, severely restricting the development of trial work.

Facing these challenges, there is no way out for the people's courts without reform. Only through reform, by gradually establishing a mechanism for independent and impartial adjudication according to law, can they meet the needs of the development of the socialist market economy and the construction of democracy and the legal system.

2. The reform of the people's courts faces favorable opportunities.

-- The development of reform, opening up, and socialist modernization provides favorable political conditions for the reform of the people's courts. The Constitutional amendment passed at the Second Session of the Ninth National People's Congress incorporated the basic strategy of governing the country according to law proposed by the Fifteenth Party Congress into the fundamental law of the state; the Resolution on the Work Report of the Supreme People's Court at that session put forward the requirement that the people's courts play an important role in governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law, laying the constitutional and legal foundation for the reform of the people's courts.

-- The gradual establishment of the socialist market economy system objectively requires the people's courts to equally protect the legitimate rights and interests of parties, handle disputes between parties fairly and promptly, combat illegal and criminal activities that infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of market entities, and reform judicial concepts, management models, and operational methods that are incompatible with economic construction and social development at the primary stage of socialism.

-- The deepening understanding of the relationship among reform, development, and stability in the whole society, the enhancement of the people's legal awareness, and extensive beneficial discussions on judicial reform in theoretical circles have gradually turned court reform into a consensus of the whole society, creating favorable social conditions for the reform of the people's courts.

-- The reforms already carried out by the people's courts have accumulated experience for further reform. In recent years, courts across the country have implemented a series of reform measures to uphold strict law enforcement and ensure judicial fairness. People's courts at all levels have fully implemented the open trial system and reformed trial methods; strengthened the responsibilities of collegial panels and sole judges, and regulated the activities of the judicial committee; gradually implemented the systems of separation of case filing and trial, separation of trial and enforcement, and separation of trial and supervision. In accordance with the Judges Law, successful practices and explorations have been carried out in areas such as judge examinations, appointments, and exchanges. These reform measures and the phased results already achieved have created favorable conditions for advancing the reform of the people's courts in the future.

Looking at the overall situation, the reform of the people's courts faces a rare historical opportunity. We must stand at the height of the times, base ourselves on reality, focus on long-term development, further emancipate our minds, seize the opportunity, forge ahead, and confidently push the reform of the people's courts deeper.

3. The reform of the people's courts must be guided by Deng Xiaoping Theory, based on the basic strategy of governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law proposed by the Fifteenth Party Congress, and the requirement to advance judicial reform, and adhere to the ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts.

4. The reform of the people's courts must always adhere to the following principles:

-- Adhere to the leadership of the Party;

-- Adhere to the state system of people's democratic dictatorship and the political system of the people's congress system;

-- Adhere to independent adjudication according to law;

-- Adhere to the unity of the national legal system;

-- Adhere to proceeding from China's actual conditions and drawing on useful foreign experience in court and judge management.

5. The overall goal of the reform of the people's courts is: Closely focusing on the development of the socialist market economy and the need to establish a socialist country under the rule of law, according to the basic principles stipulated by the Constitution and laws, improve the organizational system of the people's courts; further perfect an independent, fair, open, efficient, clean, and well-functioning trial working mechanism; under a scientific judge management system, cultivate a high-quality team of judges; establish a financial management system that guarantees the full performance of trial functions by the people's courts; and truly establish a socialist judicial system with Chinese characteristics.

6. To achieve the overall goal of the reform of the people's courts, from 1999 to 2003, the basic tasks and specific objectives to be achieved are: With the implementation of the principle of open trial as the main content, further deepen the reform of trial methods; with a focus on strengthening the responsibilities of collegial panels and judges, establish a trial management mechanism that suits the characteristics and laws of trial work; centering on strengthening trial work, reform the internal institutions of the courts, so that the forces of trial personnel and judicial administrative personnel are reasonably allocated; adhere to the principle of the Party managing cadres, further deepen the reform of the court personnel management system, and build a team of judges with strong political awareness, professional competence, and good conduct; strengthen the modernization of court office facilities, improve trial work efficiency and management level; perfect various supervision mechanisms to ensure the fairness and integrity of judicial personnel; actively explore reforms in the organizational system, court cadre management system, and court financial management system, laying the foundation for achieving the overall goal of the reform of the people's courts.

II. Basic Content of the Five-Year Reform of the People's Courts

(A) Further Deepen the Reform of Trial Methods

7. By the end of 1999, people's courts at all levels nationwide, based on the principles of clear responsibilities, reasonable division of labor, and efficient operation, shall fully implement the separation of case filing and trial, separation of trial and enforcement, and separation of trial and supervision. The separation of case filing and trial in people's tribunals shall be carried out in light of actual conditions.

8. Establish a scientific case hearing process management system, where a specialized agency, according to the different stages in the hearing process of various cases, tracks and manages different hearing stages such as case filing, service, trial, and case conclusion, ensuring the fairness and efficiency of case hearing.

9. By the end of 2000, the Supreme People's Court shall formulate standards for filing retrial cases.

10. Further improve the system of cross-examination and authentication.

-- Standardize the cross-examination system. Cross-examination is a prerequisite for the judge's correct authentication. Any evidence not cross-examined in court shall not be used as a basis for deciding a case.

-- Explore the conditions and methods for open authentication and improve the authentication system.

-- Based on summarizing experience, by the end of 2000, formulate rules on the application of evidence.

11. Take effective measures to solve the problem of witnesses, especially key witnesses, appearing in court. At the same time, summarize trial experience, study issues such as the obligation of witnesses to testify in court, personal safety, material guarantees, and legal liability, and timely submit a proposal to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for formulating a Witness Law.

12. Strictly implement the "Several Provisions on Strictly Implementing the Open Trial System" issued by the Supreme People's Court on March 8, 1999, and fully implement the open trial system. For cases tried in open court by the people's courts, the rate of judgments pronounced in court shall be gradually increased.

13. Accelerate the pace of reform of written judgments and improve the quality of written judgments. The focus of reform is to strengthen the analysis and authentication of disputed evidence in cross-examination, and enhance the reasoning of judgments; through written judgments, not only record the process of adjudication but also disclose the reasons for the judgment, making written judgments a carrier for displaying the image of judicial fairness to the public and a vivid textbook for legal education.

14. Starting from 2000, typical cases concerning the application of law discussed and decided by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court shall be published for reference by lower courts when hearing similar cases.

15. Strictly implement the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law concerning trial procedures and continue to deepen the reform of criminal trial methods.

-- Ensure according to law that a defendant has the right to defense. For cases tried under ordinary procedures, if the defendant genuinely cannot afford a defense lawyer due to financial difficulties or other reasons, the people's court shall, in accordance with the "Joint Notice on Criminal Legal Aid Work" issued by the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice, actively arrange for a designated lawyer who undertakes the obligation of legal aid to provide defense for the defendant, so as to ensure trial quality.

-- For cases of second instance, except those that may be tried without a hearing according to law, they shall be tried in open court and judgments publicly announced; for death penalty cases of second instance, if the appellant raises objections to the facts or evidence found by the court of first instance, or presents new facts or evidence, or the case has significant social impact, a hearing shall be conducted in open court according to law.

-- Based on summarizing pilot experiences for criminal retrial cases, formulate provisions for conducting hearings in criminal retrial cases.

-- The presiding judge shall strive to improve the ability to preside over and direct courtroom proceedings, pay attention to the role of prosecution and defense in courtroom argument, and ascertain the facts of the case through activities such as witnesses testifying in court, presenting evidence, cross-examination, accusation, and defense.

-- Under the premise of fully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of victims, strictly control the filing of private prosecution cases; while emphasizing the burden of proof on the parties in private prosecution cases, do a good job in guiding the parties to present evidence and necessary investigation and evidence collection.

16. The reform of civil and economic trial methods shall further improve the system of presenting evidence. In addition to continuing to adhere to the principle that the party claiming a right bears the burden of proof, establish a time limit system for presenting evidence, a system for exchanging evidence before trial for major, complex, and difficult cases, improve the system for the people's court to collect evidence, and further standardize the activities of parties in presenting evidence and cross-examination.

17. Improve administrative trial methods. Closely focus on reviewing the legality of the specific administrative act sued; completely change the practice of reviewing both the specific administrative act and the plaintiff's conduct, or even reviewing only the plaintiff's conduct; improve the rules for presenting evidence, cross-examination, and authentication in administrative litigation; establish an evidence system that suits the characteristics of administrative litigation; based on the development of administrative trial practice, further improve forms of judgment.

(B) Establish Trial Organizational Forms That Suit the Laws of Trial Work

18. Strengthen the responsibilities of collegial panels and judges, promote the system for selecting and appointing presiding judges and sole judges, and fully leverage the directive and coordinating role of presiding judges and sole judges during courtroom proceedings. By the end of 2000, clearly define the conditions and responsibilities for judges serving as presiding judges and sole judges, and establish a system for review, assessment, selection, and appointment of presiding judges and sole judges. Presiding judges and sole judges shall sign written judgments according to their trial responsibilities.

19. Within the scope prescribed by law, make greater use of summary procedures to hear cases. When conditions are ripe, submit proposals to the legislative body to amend the Criminal Procedure Law and the Civil Procedure Law, expanding the scope of cases tried by summary procedures in the people's courts.

20. On the basis of the full implementation of the system for selecting and appointing presiding judges, ensure that, except for major and difficult cases that the collegial panel, according to law, submits to the president for referral to the judicial committee for discussion and decision, all other cases shall be heard and decided by the collegial panel; the president or division chief shall not individually change the decision of the collegial panel.

21. Promote the practice of presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs participating in collegial panels and serving as presiding judges to hear cases. People's courts at all levels shall, based on their actual circumstances, set clear requirements for presidents, vice-presidents, division chiefs, and deputy division chiefs serving as presiding judges to hear cases.

22. Regulate the work responsibilities of the judicial committee. As the highest trial organization within the court, on the basis of strengthening the responsibilities of collegial panels and continuously improving the quality of case hearings, the judicial committee shall gradually limit itself to discussing the application of law in a few major, difficult, and complex cases submitted by the collegial panel to the president for referral, and summarizing trial experience, so as to fully exert its role in researching and providing authoritative guidance on fundamental and overall issues in trial work.

23. Improve the people's assessor system. On the basis of summarizing experience and fully demonstrating, submit proposals to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on issues such as the qualifications, selection procedures, scope of participation in trial cases, rights and obligations, and financial guarantees for people's assessors, so that the people's assessor system is truly implemented and strengthened (On May 8, 1999, signed by President Xiao Yang, the Supreme People's Court submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress the "Proposal on Deliberating the 'Decision on Improving the People's Assessor System (Draft)'").

(C) Scientifically Set Up Internal Institutions of the Courts

24. Further clarify the scope of responsibilities and division of labor of trial departments, changing the current situation of overlapping functions and unclear division. By the end of 2000, the Supreme People's Court shall clearly define the scope of responsibilities of trial divisions and offices.

25. Strengthen trial departments, streamline, merge, and uniformly establish judicial administrative management departments for people's courts at all levels; stipulate the ratio of trial department personnel to judicial administrative management department personnel at all levels of people's courts; properly reassign surplus personnel from judicial administrative management departments.

26. Implement the spirit of the "Report of the Party Leadership Group of the Supreme People's Court on Solving the Problem of 'Difficulty in Enforcement' by the People's Courts" forwarded in Document Zhong Fa [1999] No. 11, and reform the enforcement institutions and enforcement work system of the people's courts.

-- By the end of 1999, high people's courts of each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government shall implement a system of unified management and coordination of enforcement work of people's courts within their jurisdictions. The enforcement agency of the high people's court shall be responsible for coordinating and handling enforcement dispute cases with enforcement agencies of high people's courts outside its jurisdiction.

-- Strengthen the construction of enforcement teams. Continue the rectification work of enforcement teams, promptly transfer personnel unsuitable for enforcement work out of enforcement positions; ensure that qualified enforcement personnel are allocated in a proportion of no less than 15% of the total existing authorized staffing. Strengthen scientific management of enforcement teams, strictly enforce enforcement discipline, intensify professional training, and improve law enforcement standards. As soon as possible, build a nationwide enforcement team that is politically steadfast, honest and clean, strictly disciplined, professionally proficient, with a strong work style, and well-trained.

-- When conditions are ripe, through pilot projects, establish a nationwide enforcement work system that provides unified leadership, effective supervision and coordination, and efficient operation for enforcement agencies of people's courts at all levels.

-- Based on summarizing enforcement work experience, draft an Enforcement Law and submit it to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for deliberation as soon as possible.

27. Based on the principle of facilitating litigation by the parties and facilitating trial of cases by the people's courts, and in accordance with the requirements of standardization and scale, reasonably set up people's tribunals. Local courts shall, based on investigation and research and according to actual local conditions, formulate development goals and plans for the construction of people's tribunals in a practical manner.

-- Each people's tribunal shall be staffed with at least three judges and one clerk; judicial police may be deployed where conditions permit. In economically developed areas with good road traffic conditions, some tribunals shall be systematically abolished and reorganized or merged into people's tribunals of a certain scale;

-- By the end of 1999, complete the cleanup, adjustment, and abolition of existing "specialized tribunals" and people's tribunals that do not meet conditions or are not conducive to independent and impartial exercise of adjudicative power according to law;

-- By the end of 2000, abolish people's tribunals within urban districts.

28. Regulate the management system of unified leadership for judicial police. Earnestly implement the provisions of "dual leadership, formation management" stipulated in the "Interim Regulations on Judicial Police of the People's Courts," strengthen unified management and deployment; explore reforms to the appointment system for judicial police, pilot part-time employment of some judicial police, and smooth the channels for entry and exit of judicial police.

29. Reform and rationalize the forensic identification and information work systems of the people's courts. Concentrate human resources, funds, and technology, focusing on high people's courts, to establish forensic identification institutions; the Supreme People's Court shall establish the People's Court Forensic Identification Center; gradually promote the establishment of a unified forensic identification system; uniformly set up information institutions such as communications and statistics.

(D) Deepen the Reform of the Court Personnel Management System

30. Strictly implement the "Decision on Further Strengthening the Construction of the Contingent of Political and Legal Cadres" of the CPC Central Committee. The Party leadership group of the higher people's court shall actively and proactively cooperate with local Party committees to strengthen the co-management role in the leading group members of lower courts, and fully leverage the function of Party leadership groups of people's courts at all levels in managing cadres.

31. Summarize the practice carried out in some regions since 1988 where the leadership group members of local courts were mainly managed by the Party leadership group of the higher people's court, assisted by the local Party committee; affirm the results achieved in the pilots; earnestly study the problems existing in the pilots; and propose solutions.

32. Reform the source channels of judges. Gradually establish a system for selecting judges of higher people's courts from outstanding judges of lower people's courts and from lawyers and highly qualified legal professionals. Graduates of law schools and other personnel who have passed open examinations shall first be assigned to intermediate and basic-level people's courts. After five years, trial divisions of high people's courts and the Supreme People's Court shall select judges from lower courts and high-level legal professionals in society. This will truly create a virtuous cycle in the source and selection of judges, ensuring the requirement of a high-quality team of judges.

33. With the development of the selection and appointment of presiding judges, and in conjunction with the amendment of the Organic Law of the People's Courts, high people's courts may conduct pilot projects on equipping judges with judge assistants and abolishing assistant judge positions, to explore experience.

34. Conduct research on the establishment of fixed judge staffing for people's courts at all levels. Under the premise of ensuring trial quality and efficiency, determine judge staffing in a planned and step-by-step manner.

-- Select some courts in different regions and at different levels to conduct pilot projects on judge staffing;

-- Based on summarizing the experience of pilot courts and conducting in-depth investigation and research, the Supreme People's Court shall, in 2001, consult with the Central Organization Department and Personnel Department to propose a specific plan for judge staffing.

35. Further strengthen and improve the judge exchange and rotation system.

-- In principle, judge exchanges shall be conducted across different regions within the court system or between higher-level and lower-level courts. Job rotation shall be premised on not affecting the specialization of judges and on the principle of not disrupting trial work.

-- Implement a system of tenure avoidance and exchange for leading cadres in courts. The presidents of local courts at all levels shall serve in a different location from that of their long-term residence; the vice presidents shall implement a system of rotating their areas of responsibility; positions of chief judges of similar trial divisions shall be subject to regular rotation. Through the implementation of judge exchange and rotation systems, a positive interaction among judges and a rational allocation of personnel shall be achieved.

36. Strengthen the training of judges. The Supreme People's Court and each Higher People's Court shall, by 2001, complete a rotational training of all presidents, vice presidents, chief judges, and deputy chief judges of Intermediate People's Courts and above, and of Primary People's Courts. Within two years, each Higher People's Court shall transform the functions of its branch of the National Judges College, and establish a judges' college or other judge training institution on that basis. After 2001, judges must undergo full-time off-the-job training at the National Judges College or other judge training institutions every three years; newly appointed judges must undergo full-time off-the-job training to learn specialized legal knowledge and trial practice skills.

37. Establish a separate job sequence for court clerks. On the basis of summarizing pilot experiences, the Supreme People's Court, in conjunction with relevant departments, shall formulate administrative measures for court clerks in 2000, and fully establish this system after 2001.

(V) Strengthen the modernization of court office facilities, further improve judicial efficiency and court management standards.

38. People's courts at all levels shall regard strengthening office modernization and other material equipment construction, and improving court management standards, as important aspects of improving law enforcement conditions, enhancing trial quality and efficiency, and achieving judicial impartiality, and shall earnestly and diligently pursue these tasks.

-- Adapt to the needs of trial method reform, and further improve the construction of trial courtrooms. Promptly resolve the problems of insufficient trial courtrooms and supporting facilities. Trial courtrooms shall be equipped with corresponding technical equipment such as security inspection systems, courtroom text input, audio recording, video recording, projection, and closed-circuit television monitoring systems.

-- By the end of 2001, basically achieve the application of modern technological means such as computers in trial records, production of litigation documents, court personnel management, archive management, and statistical data information processing. Accelerate the construction of computer information networks and communications, and unify network application software. Within three years, achieve computer networking between the Supreme People's Court and higher and intermediate people's courts; strive to establish a national court computer network system within five years, incorporating case management, information and statistical data collection, and transmission into the network system, thereby increasing the technological content of various management tasks in people's courts.

39. By the end of 2000, the Supreme People's Court shall complete the reform of the judicial statistical indicator system for all types of cases. Further explore the establishment of a modern judicial statistics and management system that meets the needs of people's court trial work management, with rapid response and macro-analysis capabilities.

(VI) Strengthen institutional development, improve supervision mechanisms, and ensure judicial impartiality and integrity.

40. Establish effective internal restraint mechanisms.

-- Strictly enforce the trial supervision system, further strengthen the authority, accuracy, and effectiveness of supervision by higher-level people's courts over the trials of lower-level people's courts.

-- Fully implement the "Measures for Investigating Accountability for Illegal Adjudication by Judicial Personnel of the People's Courts (Trial)" and the "Measures for Disciplinary Sanctions for Judicial Personnel of the People's Courts (Trial)," effectively strengthen disciplinary supervision over trial work, and rigorously investigate and punish various illegal and disciplinary acts involving the exercise of trial authority.

-- Further improve the supervisor system. By the end of 1999, each Higher People's Court shall establish a supervisor system, fully leveraging the role of supervisors in supervising, inspecting, investigating, and guiding court work. By amending the "Organic Law of the People's Courts," the work of supervisors in people's courts shall be legalized, trial discipline shall be implemented institutionally, and the professional ethics of judges shall be further strengthened.

-- Improve and strengthen the trial supervision working mechanism. Formulate several provisions on strengthening trial supervision work in 2000.

41. By the end of 1999, formulate regulations concerning the relationship between judicial personnel of people's courts and parties, defense counsel, and lawyers during litigation proceedings.

42. Formulate normative opinions on people's courts accepting social supervision, so that the acceptance of social supervision by people's courts becomes institutionalized, proceduralized, and legalized.

-- Fully implement the "Several Opinions on People's Courts Accepting Supervision by the People's Congresses and Their Standing Committees."

-- Further standardize the work of people's courts accepting legal supervision by the People's Procuratorates, especially in the trial of civil, economic, and administrative protest cases.

-- In conjunction with relevant departments, formulate regulations on the acceptance of news supervision over the trial work of people's courts.

(VII) Actively explore deeper-level reforms of the people's courts.

43. Proceeding from the requirements of maintaining the unity of the national legal system and achieving judicial impartiality, actively explore the reform of the organizational system of people's courts. In 2001, submit a proposal to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to amend the "Organic Law of the People's Courts," gradually establishing an organizational system for people's courts that conforms to China's political system and ensures that courts independently and impartially exercise their adjudicative power according to law.

-- Conduct research on the establishment of a maritime high court;

-- Conduct research on the legal status, management system, and jurisdiction of courts for railways, forestry, agriculture, etc. Gradually change the current situation where courts for railways, agricultural reclamation, forestry, oil fields, and ports are led and managed by administrative departments or enterprises.

44. In accordance with the requirements of safeguarding legal authority and judicial unity, actively explore the reform of the personnel management system for people's courts, to better realize the leadership of the Party and the supervision of the People's Congress.

45. On the basis of fully implementing the "two lines of revenue and expenditure" regulations, explore the establishment of a court funding guarantee system to ensure the necessary funding for the performance of trial functions.

III. Strengthen leadership, gradually achieve reform goals.

46. People's courts at all levels must strengthen organizational leadership and unswervingly implement the various reform tasks set forth in this Outline. In accordance with the reform measures and goals set in the Outline, and in light of local actual conditions, they shall respectively formulate specific implementation plans for their own departments and regions. A mid-term evaluation of the people's court reforms shall be conducted in 2001; a summary of the implementation of the Outline shall be conducted in 2003.

47. When formulating specific reform implementation plans in light of local conditions, people's courts at all levels shall extensively solicit opinions from the masses and relevant parties, adhere to the principle of coming from the masses and going to the masses, encourage the airing of views, and choose the good and follow it.

48. Based on the present and considering the long term, identify the key reform priorities for the near term. Reform measures identified in the Outline that do not require legislation or legal amendments to be carried out, especially reforms such as trial methods, internal court institutions, trial organizations, and the separate job sequence for court clerks, shall be included in the near-term reform goals, initiated as soon as possible, and implemented promptly.

49. The reform of the people's courts is a comprehensive reform ranging from judicial concepts, working methods, and management mechanisms to judicial systems, and is an important task affecting the overall trial work. While actively implementing the reform measures set forth in the Outline, people's courts at all levels shall actively conduct theoretical research and propaganda work on some major, deeper-level reform issues, making full theoretical and public opinion preparations for achieving the overall goal of people's court reform, and laying a solid foundation.

50. In the course of the reform, the Supreme People's Court shall, based on the progress of the national economic system reform and political system reform, as well as the new situations and new problems faced in the people's court reform, make appropriate modifications, supplements, and improvements to the reform goals and content, so as to adapt to the needs of changing circumstances.

The "Five-Year Reform Outline for the People's Courts," as an action plan to organize and mobilize national people's courts at all levels to advance judicial reform, clarifies the direction of people's court reform and is of great significance. Achieving the various reform goals set forth in the Outline will give the people's courts a new look and effectively promote the implementation of the strategy of governing the country according to law. People's courts at all levels, under the leadership of the Party Central Committee with Comrade Jiang Zemin at its core, holding high the great banner of Deng Xiaoping Theory, shall further boost their spirits, work solidly, forge ahead, boldly innovate, and courageously practice, striving to fully realize the various reform tasks set forth in the Outline and build a socialist country ruled by law!

October 20, 1999

Explanation of the "Five-Year Reform Outline for the People's Courts"

Zhu Mingshan

(October 20, 1999)

In order to implement the basic strategy of governing the country according to law determined at the 15th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, and to actively and steadily advance the reform of the people's courts, the Supreme People's Court, after sufficient investigation and research, soliciting opinions, and ten drafts, formulated the "Five-Year Reform Outline for the People's Courts" (hereinafter referred to as the "Outline").

I. On the Necessity of Deepening the Reform of the People's Courts

After the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, in order to meet the needs of socialist modernization and democratic legal construction, the reform of the people's courts was also actively carried out. The establishment of trial institutions was increasingly perfected, the reform of trial methods achieved remarkable results, and beneficial explorations were also conducted in personnel system reform. However, it should also be recognized that with the establishment of China's socialist market economy system and the implementation of the basic strategy of governing the country according to law, the past reforms of the people's courts, whether in depth or breadth, can no longer meet the needs of the development of the new situation. Continuing to deepen the reform of the people's courts is imperative.

Continuing to deepen the reform of the people's courts is an objective need for the establishment and development of the socialist market economy. In the process of transforming from a planned economy to a socialist market economy, due to changes in social and economic relations, adjustments in interest patterns, and the intertwining of old and new social contradictions, various types of cases brought to the people's courts have increased substantially, with new types of cases increasing and the difficulty of handling them increasing. Because the current management system and trial working mechanism of the people's courts cannot fully adapt to changes in the situation, a large number of cases brought to the people's courts are difficult to handle promptly and fairly. Driven by interests, local protectionism that divides the unified market has emerged in some areas, seriously interfering with the trial work of the people's courts. However, the localized characteristics of the current court management system make it difficult to overcome local protectionism in judicial activities.

Continuing to deepen the reform of the people's courts is necessary for building a socialist country ruled by law. As the judicial organ of the state, the people's courts exercise the adjudicative power on behalf of the state according to law, symbolizing social justice and embodying the spirit of fairness. The official acts of judges represent the image of a country ruled by law and reflect the level of governing the country according to law. Higher and stricter requirements should be placed on them. However, the current judge management system is not conducive to improving the overall quality of the judge contingent, nor is it conducive to the independent adjudication of the people's courts according to law.

Continuing to deepen the reform of the people's courts is necessary for the self-development of trial work. With the development of the socialist market economy, not only has the number of various cases brought to the people's courts today continued to increase, but the types of cases have also developed from past criminal and civil cases to criminal, civil, economic, administrative, intellectual property, maritime, and commercial cases. However, the administration of trial work is bureaucratized, violating the laws of trial work and affecting the fair and efficient handling of various types of cases; the financial difficulties of people's courts, especially primary people's courts, backward equipment, and inadequate material support also severely restrict the development of the people's courts.

Continuing to deepen the reform of the people's courts is an inevitable requirement of the continuous improvement of the legal awareness of the broad masses of the people. With the smooth progress of China's socialist modernization and democratic legal construction, especially the smooth development of the "Third Five-Year" legal education campaign, the cultural literacy and legal awareness of the masses have greatly improved, awareness of fairness and justice has become significantly stronger, and more and more legal actions are being taken to protect their legitimate rights and interests using legal means. Under such objective circumstances, the people's courts must seize the opportunity to reform and establish an independent and fair trial working mechanism according to law.

The "Outline" is put forward under the guidance of the above ideas, meeting the needs of deepening the reform of the people's courts. After discussion, revision, and promulgation, it will certainly promote the deepening of the reform of the people's courts and achieve greater results.

II. On the Principles to be Adhered to in the Reform of the People's Courts

The judicial reform of the people's courts is an important part of China's political system reform. In order to grasp the correct direction of the reform, Article 4 of the "Outline" sets forth the principles that the people's courts should adhere to in the reform:

Must adhere to the leadership of the Party. The Communist Party of China is the leading core of China's socialist cause and the fundamental guarantee for the healthy development of the people's court reform in the correct political direction. Without the leadership of the Party, the reform of the people's courts will inevitably deviate from the correct direction and track; without the leadership of the Party, the reform of the people's courts cannot succeed. Adhering to the leadership of the Party means resolutely implementing the Party's basic line and the basic strategy of governing the country according to law proposed at the 15th National Congress; it means, under the premise of resolutely implementing the Party's principles and policies, emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts, boldly innovating, and courageously pioneering. The reform of the people's courts must be carried out under the leadership of the Party, and any practice that violates this principle should be firmly opposed.

Must adhere to the system of people's congresses. The People's Congress is the fundamental political system of our country, which is essentially different from the "separation of powers" system implemented in Western capitalist countries. Under the system of people's congresses, the people's courts are created by and are responsible to the people's congresses. At the same time, the people's courts independently exercise their adjudicative power according to law, free from interference by any administrative organ, social organization, or individual. The reform of the people's courts must be conducive to the people's congresses and their standing committees strengthening supervision over the people's courts. Any practice that weakens or impairs the supervision of the people's congresses is wrong.

Should adhere to the principle of national legal unity. China is a unitary state. Legal unity is a basic feature of this state structure. Local people's courts at all levels are courts established by the state locally, not "local courts." Through reform, a guarantee mechanism for independent and impartial adjudication according to law should be established. The Supreme People's Court and local people's courts at all levels should strictly implement the national constitution and laws, resolutely safeguard the unity of the socialist legal system, make the people's courts truly national courts, and prevent local people's courts from becoming tools of local protectionism.

In addition, in the reform, the people's courts should also adhere to the principle of proceeding from China's national conditions and drawing on beneficial foreign experiences in the management of courts and judges, so that the reform of the people's courts advances along the correct track.

III. On Further Deepening the Reform of Trial Methods

Since the 1996 "National Conference on Trial Method Reform of Courts," people's courts at all levels have earnestly implemented the spirit of this conference, carried out extensive explorations around the implementation of the open trial system and trial method reform, and achieved remarkable results. However, development is very uneven across regions. In a few places, there has been little progress to date; in some places, there has even been regression. Even in places where the reforms have been relatively successful, there are still issues that need further improvement and deepening. Therefore, deepening the reform of trial methods remains an important topic in current court reform. The "Outline" emphasizes the following aspects regarding trial method reform:

First, strengthening the responsibilities of trial organizations. Article 18 of the "Outline" stipulates: "Implement the collegiate bench responsibility system, strengthen the responsibilities of the collegiate bench and judges, and promote the selection system for judges serving as presiding judges and sole judges." The presiding judge plays a very important role in cases tried by the collegiate bench. To a certain extent, the level of the presiding judge represents the level of the collegiate bench. To ensure the quality of case handling and improve work efficiency, promoting the selection system for presiding judges and sole judges, and establishing a trial organization operating mechanism that can both give full play to the leading role of the presiding judge and concentrate the collective wisdom of the collegiate bench, is very important. After implementing the selection system for presiding judges and sole judges, when the collegiate bench or sole judge panel makes a ruling on a case in accordance with their trial duties, the presiding judge and sole judge shall issue litigation documents according to law. Judicial personnel selected as presiding judges or sole judges shall be given priority over other judges with similar qualifications when being promoted in judge rank, so as to fully mobilize their work enthusiasm and enhance their sense of professionalism and responsibility.

Article 22 of the "Outline" stipulates the duties of the adjudication committee. In order to give full play to the role of the adjudication committee as the highest trial organization within the court and implement the principle of direct adjudication, proceeding from China's current actual situation, the "Outline" proposes that the adjudication committee should gradually be limited to discussing only the application of law in a small number of major, difficult, and complex cases submitted by the collegiate bench at the request of the court president. The responsibility for fact-finding in cases shall rest with the collegiate bench. The adjudication committee should strengthen the summary of trial work experience, conduct research on fundamental and overall issues, and provide authoritative guidance.

The selection system for presiding judges and sole judges proposed in the "Outline" is different from the presiding judge responsibility system. According to law, people's courts try cases using the collegiate system. Although the presiding judge plays an irreplaceable role in the trial of cases, the collegiate bench must adhere to the principle of the minority being subordinate to the majority. The presiding judge cannot exclude the opinions of other members of the collegiate bench, nor can he replace the opinions of the majority of the collegiate bench with his own opinions. If the presiding judge has a significant disagreement with the opinions of other members of the collegiate bench, he shall submit the matter to the court president for referral to the adjudication committee for discussion and decision. At the same time, the court president and division chief are not a level of trial organization and cannot personally change the decision of the collegiate bench. As the responsibilities of the collegiate bench are gradually strengthened, the practice of court leaders and division chiefs specifically approving cases will be gradually weakened. In addition to being responsible for the administrative affairs of the court or trial division, the court leaders and division chiefs at all levels of people's courts shall also genuinely fulfill their duties as judges by serving as presiding judges in collegiate benches and trying a certain number of cases each year. At the same time, they shall provide guidance on trial work by presiding over discussions of a small number of major, difficult, and complex cases, spot-checking effective judgments, investigating and researching new situations and new problems, and summarizing trial work experience.

Second, fully implement the "three separations." The implementation of the separation of case filing and trial, the separation of trial and enforcement, and the separation of trial and supervision in the trial work of the people's courts is conducive to maintaining judicial fairness and is an objective requirement of the laws of trial work. Article 7 of the "Outline" stipulates: "By the end of 1999, all people's courts nationwide shall fully implement the separation of case filing and trial, the separation of trial and enforcement, and the separation of trial and supervision, based on the principles of clear responsibilities, reasonable division of labor, and efficient operation." Currently, the work on the "three separations" is basically complete in most courts, with remarkable results. The active promotion of case trial process management by some courts, where specialized agencies arrange and track trial stages such as case filing, service of process, court sessions, and case conclusion, is a beneficial exploration of the trial work management model, which has positive significance for ensuring procedural fairness, improving trial efficiency, strengthening trial supervision, and promoting clean government. To implement the provisions of the "Outline," people's courts at all levels shall focus on implementing the separation of institutions and functions, improving institutions, clarifying responsibilities, straightening out relationships, and solving the problem of overlapping functions of trial departments; they shall establish and improve relevant systems, gradually forming a set of operating methods to ensure fair, efficient, and standardized case trial, and improving various supervision and restraint mechanisms in trial work; they shall focus on practical results and avoid formalism, so that the "three separations" truly play their role.

Third, further deepening the reform of trial methods. The reform of trial methods is the central focus of the reform of the trial methods of the People's Courts. To further improve the reform of trial methods, Articles 10 and 11 of the Outline provide for issues such as cross-examination, authentication, and the appearance of witnesses in court. The current focus of the reform of trial methods is to comprehensively implement the three major procedural laws and further improve the criminal, civil, and administrative trial methods.

The reform of criminal trial methods should focus on the prominent issues existing in criminal trial work and mainly resolve the following issues: First, ensure according to law that the defendant has the right to obtain a defense. For cases tried under ordinary procedures, if the defendant truly cannot afford to retain a defense lawyer due to financial difficulties or other reasons, the People's Court shall, in accordance with the Joint Notice on Criminal Legal Aid Work, appoint a lawyer who undertakes the obligation of legal aid to provide a defense for him; during the trial process, the judges must not only pay attention to the opinions of the prosecution but also note the reasons of the defense, and strive to improve their ability to control and direct the trial. Second, gradually increase the rate of open trials for cases at second instance and retrial cases. The reform of trial methods involves all aspects of the People's Courts' trial of cases, including the first instance procedure, the second instance procedure, and the trial supervision procedure. People's Courts at all levels must conduct open trials and public pronouncements of judgments in cases at second instance, except where law permits trial without an open hearing. In particular, for death penalty cases, if the defendant raises objections to the facts or evidence determined in the first instance, or presents new facts or evidence, or the case has significant social impact, an open trial must be held. This is a step forward from the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, with the aim of making death penalty cases watertight. Currently, retrial cases in criminal proceedings generally are not tried with an open hearing. Although there are many objective reasons for this, such practice is not conducive to ensuring the quality of case handling or to correcting erroneous judgments. The Supreme People's Court must actively coordinate with relevant departments and, on the basis of summarizing pilot experiences, formulate provisions for the open trial of criminal retrial cases as soon as possible, to promote the conduct of open trials in criminal retrial cases. Third, attach importance to the reform of trial methods in private prosecution cases. After the amendment of the Criminal Procedure Law, the number of criminal private prosecution cases accepted by the People's Courts has increased significantly, involving a wide range of charges, becoming an important aspect of criminal trial work. Currently, there are many problems in the filing review and evidence determination of criminal private prosecution cases tried by the courts. While fully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of victims, the People's Courts must strictly review the filing of criminal private prosecution cases, emphasize the litigant's burden of proof, and actively guide litigants to provide evidence. When necessary, judges may conduct necessary investigations and evidence collection based on the circumstances of the case, to improve the trial quality of criminal private prosecution cases.

Through years of practice, the reform of civil and economic trial methods of the People's Courts has basically achieved that litigants can say what they want in the courtroom, present evidence for cross-examination in the courtroom, and argue their reasons in the courtroom. However, there is still insufficient public authentication and reasoning in the courtroom. Article 16 of the Outline stipulates: To focus on public authentication and on-the-spot reasoning, further improve the system of presenting evidence and cross-examination. Any evidence not cross-examined in court cannot be used as the basis for deciding the case. For major, complex, and difficult civil and economic cases, pre-trial exchange of evidence may be piloted. On the basis of investigation and research, the Supreme People's Court shall formulate provisions on the time limit for litigants to complete the presentation of evidence, the requirements for cross-examination during trial, and the basic rules for authentication. During the trial process, where the court can authenticate and reason on the spot, it should do so; if it cannot authenticate and reason on the spot, it must explain and clearly state the basis for authentication and the reasons for the judgment in the court pronouncement and the judgment document, to further improve the trial quality of civil and economic cases and ensure judicial fairness.

Improving the administrative trial methods must closely focus on examining the legality of the specific administrative act under review, and completely change the erroneous practice of examining both the specific administrative act and the plaintiff's conduct, or even examining only the plaintiff's conduct. The burden of proof for the specific administrative act lies with the defendant, which is a basic requirement of the Administrative Procedure Law and an important means of promoting administrative organs to act according to law. However, in trial practice, some courts violate the law by seeking legal basis for the specific administrative acts of administrative organs, or even requiring the plaintiff to bear the burden of proof. This violates the law and must be corrected. The forms of judgment should be further improved based on the development of administrative trial practice.

Fourth, accelerating the pace of reform of litigation documents and improving the quality of litigation documents. Judgment documents and rulings are the embodiment of the People's Courts' exercise of national adjudicative power and the ultimate carrier of judicial fairness. They should not only reflect the fairness of the People's Courts' judgment in the conclusion but also make the parties know and understand why the judgment is fair through thorough reasoning. Trial openness requires improving the rules for presenting evidence, cross-examination, and authentication in administrative litigation, and establishing evidence judgments that conform to the characteristics of administrative litigation. Only when the reasons for the judgment are made public can it be deemed final and substantive. To be able to articulate the reasons for the judgment clearly is also not easily achieved. For a long time, our judgment documents have been uniform in format, lacking authentication and reasoning, making it impossible to see the formation process of the judgment result, and lacking persuasiveness. Such judgment documents, even if there is no error in finding facts and applying the law, sometimes cannot convince the parties, often causing some parties to engage in vexatious litigation, failing to achieve good social results. At the same time, it also prevents some judges from improving their professional skills in writing judgment documents over a long period of time. Article 13 of the Outline clearly defines the focus and purpose of the reform of judgment documents. In April this year, the Supreme People's Court issued the Style of Court Criminal Litigation Documents (Sample), which all levels of People's Courts must strictly implement. The Supreme People's Court is collecting model texts of various types of litigation documents for public publication to guide the writing of litigation documents in courts nationwide. People's Courts at all levels may promote the development of litigation document reform through seminars and evaluation meetings on litigation documents.

IV. Regarding the Scientific Establishment of Internal Organs of the People's Courts

Currently, the establishment of internal organs within the People's Courts is not entirely reasonable. The main manifestations are overlapping functions, redundant institutions, a disproportionately large proportion of judicial administrative personnel on the payroll, and low efficiency, which directly affects the conduct of trial work. To this end, Articles 24 and 25 of the Outline propose to further clarify the scope of responsibilities and division of work of trial departments; streamline and merge functionally overlapping judicial administrative management departments; and determine a reform plan for the personnel ratio between trial departments and judicial administrative management departments. Regarding the determination of the ratio of personnel in trial departments to those in judicial administrative management departments, there were differing opinions in the discussion. Several earlier drafts of the Outline had proposed a ratio. However, considering the uneven economic development across different regions and the significant differences in the ratios of trial and administrative personnel due to different internal organs established by People's Courts at various levels, it is difficult to scientifically determine a ratio without extensive investigation and research. Therefore, the Outline only makes flexible provisions, pending further in-depth investigation and research on this issue before making clear and specific provisions.

Once this work is determined, there will inevitably be the issue of redistributing surplus personnel from the judicial administrative management departments. People's Courts at all levels should seize this opportunity to optimize the structure of their cadres. For judicial administrative personnel who hold trial titles and, after assessment, possess certain trial business capabilities and are competent for trial work, they should be assigned to relevant trial divisions according to their expertise. Personnel who are not suitable for trial work should undergo a period of training, followed by a strict assessment, and be assigned appropriate work. Personnel who do not pass the assessment should be firmly transferred out of the court.

Regarding the reform of the enforcement work system of the People's Courts. In accordance with the spirit of the Report of the Party Group of the Supreme People's Court on Resolving the Problem of "Difficulty in Enforcement" of the People's Courts, forwarded by Document Zhongfa [1999] No. 11, Article 26 of the Outline proposes that by the end of this year, enforcement work within each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government should implement a system of unified management and coordination. Unified management and unified coordination require not only that the enforcement organs of the higher People's Courts supervise, inspect, and evaluate the enforcement cases handled by the lower People's Courts, and coordinate to resolve cases with enforcement difficulties or disputes, but also that they bear the responsibility of supervising the personnel composition and performance of duties of the enforcement organs of the lower People's Courts. In recent times, some Higher People's Courts have taken the lead and established a system within their court system where higher People's Courts exercise unified management and coordination over the enforcement work of lower People's Courts. Higher People's Courts with the conditions should also promptly study and, together with relevant departments, formulate specific implementation plans to create conditions for further deepening the reform of the enforcement work system of courts nationwide.

V. Regarding Actively Exploring a Modern Judge Management Model with Chinese Characteristics

Establishing a modern judge management model that conforms to the laws of trial work and has Chinese characteristics, and cultivating a high-quality team of judges reflecting professional requirements, is not only necessary for the People's Courts to exercise adjudicative power independently and impartially according to law, but also a requirement for establishing a socialist country governed by the rule of law. To this end, Articles 32 to 34 of the Outline propose issues concerning reforming the source channels of judges, setting up judge assistants, and determining the authorized strength of judges.

Regarding reforming the source channels of judges. For many years, the People's Courts have continued to use the current method of selecting judges from within the court's own personnel. Court clerks, after a certain number of years, are promoted to assistant judges; assistant judges, after several years, are appointed as judges. This method of selecting judges is not only detrimental to broadly absorbing talent and improving the quality of the judge team, but also unfavorable to the stability and improvement of the level of other professional personnel within the court, and is one of the important reasons for the current large number and low quality of judges. In response to the above issues, Article 32 of the Outline clearly proposes "gradually establishing a system where judges of higher People's Courts are selected from outstanding judges of lower People's Courts and from lawyers and high-level legal talents." The aim is to open up new sources and selection channels for judges to achieve the goal of building a high-quality judge team.

Regarding the work of determining the authorized strength of judges. For a long time, the People's Courts only had cadres' authorized strength, not judges' authorized strength. With the continuous increase in the number of cases accepted by the People's Courts, the team of trial personnel has also gradually expanded. From 1988 to 1998, the number of cases of various types accepted by the People's Courts increased from 1.65 million to 5.88 million, 2.33 times the original; the number of trial personnel expanded from 130,000 to over 170,000, an increase of nearly 43%. Currently, the contradiction between heavy trial tasks and insufficient manpower is quite prominent. In response to such a situation, some courts have proposed continuing to expand the court's authorized strength and increase the number of judges; but some courts, after research, have proposed that currently, the number of judges in the courts is not too few but too many, and judges must improve their quality and pursue an elite path. From the actual situation, courts that piloted the selection of elite judges have seen significant improvements in the quality and efficiency of trial work. The main way to resolve the contradiction between tasks and strength lies in improving the overall quality of the judge team. Currently, there are quite a number of people who are qualified as judges but are not in trial positions, but engaged in party affairs, personnel, judicial administration, or logistics work. Judgeship has become a form of treatment, losing its intended meaning. This situation must change. Therefore, the Outline proposes to conduct research on the work of determining the authorized strength of judges in People's Courts at all levels, and under the premise of ensuring trial quality and efficiency, to determine the authorized strength of judges in a planned and step-by-step manner. This is to fundamentally solve the problems of judges not engaging in trials and the low quality of judges. Through the determination of the authorized strength of judges, trial personnel with higher quality and who truly meet the conditions will be designated as judges; those who do not meet the conditions can only do other work, such as serving as judge assistants to assist judges in their work. Of course, the work of determining the authorized strength of judges is currently still in the research stage. Higher People's Courts may, in accordance with the requirements set out in the Outline, select eligible courts within their jurisdiction to carry out pilot work on determining the authorized strength of judges, to create experience for this reform in courts nationwide.

VI. Regarding Improving the People's Assessor System

Article 23 of the Outline clearly proposes the requirements for improving the People's Assessor System. The participation of People's Assessors in trial activities is a manifestation of the People's Courts' trial work following the mass line, and is a requirement for judicial democracy in modern society and countries governed by the rule of law. Practice shows that implementing the People's Assessor System is conducive to ascertaining the facts of a case and making correct judgments; facilitates acceptance of supervision by the masses, preventing judicial corruption; helps to expand the social effects of trial activities, and will also promote the masses to receive legal education and enhance their concept of the rule of law. In recent years, some courts, without violating the Constitution and legal provisions, have actively explored and boldly attempted to reform the People's Assessor System, playing a positive role in further adhering to and improving the People's Assessor System. After thorough investigation and research, the Supreme People's Court has submitted a bill to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress proposing the reform of the People's Assessor System in China, covering the scope of cases for People's Assessors to participate in, the qualifications for serving as People's Assessors, the rights and obligations of People's Assessors, and protections, and has drafted the Decision on Improving the People's Assessor System (Draft), which was submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on May 8. To ensure a smoother implementation after the decision is passed, starting now, People's Courts at all levels should carry out investigations and surveys on the People's Assessor teams, determine management institutions, establish and improve management systems, and create favorable working conditions for People's Assessors to perform their duties according to law, solidly implementing this reform measure.

VII. Regarding Reforming the Management System for Court Clerks

With the continuous deepening of the reform of trial methods in the People's Courts, the auxiliary role of court clerks in trial work has become increasingly evident. However, for many years, we have neglected the professional requirements of the clerk's work. The management, allocation, and use of clerks have been arbitrary and rigid. The promotion system is unreasonable, and personnel turnover is high, making it impossible to ensure the stability of the clerk team. To solve this problem, Article 37 of the Outline establishes the reform measure of establishing a separate job sequence for court clerks in the People's Courts. Currently, the Supreme People's Court is studying and formulating management measures for court clerks of the People's Courts, striving to introduce them by the end of the year. As auxiliary personnel in the trial work of the People's Courts, the educational requirements for the qualifications of court clerks may be appropriately lower than those for trial personnel in the Judges Law. Regarding the issue of promoting court clerks to assistant judges, we have studied it and propose handling it according to different circumstances: For those who served as court clerks before the implementation of the management measures for court clerks of the People's Courts and meet the conditions for being a judge, they should pass the first-instance judge qualification examination before the end of 2001 and be appointed trial titles; for those who serve as court clerks after 2002, because the qualification requirements for court clerks are lower than those for judges, they may not participate in the first-instance judge qualification examination (except for those who meet the conditions for being a judge). The purpose of the reform is to establish a professional and stable team of court clerks, so that the quality of judges and court clerks can be significantly improved. After the reform, the ranks and levels of court clerks should be increased, be more reasonable and scientific compared to the higher requirements placed on their work, and help encourage and retain high-level court clerks to be content with doing a good job in trial support work.

VIII. Regarding Standardizing and Reforming the Management System of Judicial Police

In 1995, with the approval of the Central Establishment Commission, the judicial police departments were formally included in the establishment of People's Courts at all levels as internal organs of the People's Courts; in 1997, the Supreme People's Court adopted the Interim Regulations on Judicial Police of the People's Courts, which clearly specified that judicial police operate under a management system of "dual leadership and formation management"; the establishment of the police dispatch order system further strengthened the management of judicial police, generally achieving smooth command and orderly execution. However, from the current situation, there are still some urgent issues in judicial police work, mainly manifested as insufficient police strength, the personnel allocation for judicial police not matching the work they are supposed to undertake, severely impacting work development; unclear channels for entry and exit of judicial police, overall low quality; no unified management, resulting in dispersed police strength, making it difficult to fully play the due functional role of judicial police. In response to the problems in the judicial police management system, Article 28 of the Outline proposes to standardize the management system of unified leadership for judicial police and points out the reform direction of "exploring the reform of the appointment system for judicial police, piloting a part-time appointment system for some judicial police, and smoothing the channels for entry and exit of judicial police." The aim is to further clarify the work responsibilities of judicial police, standardize and strengthen the unified management and dispatch of judicial police. Regarding the pilot of a part-time appointment system for some judicial police, it is mainly to solve the problem of smooth entry and exit channels for judicial police. First, policies allow it; second, the public security system has implemented it for many years, providing a precedent; third, some courts have already applied for local administrative and institutional establishment, so there is no difficulty in establishment. After gaining experience from the pilot, a foundation will be laid for formulating professional personnel management measures for courts nationwide that meet the trial work needs of the People's Courts and conform to the professional characteristics of judicial police.

IX. Strengthening Leadership, Actively and Steadily Advancing the Reform of the People's Courts

The ongoing reform of the People's Courts involves not only the previous judicial concepts, habitual working methods, and outdated management systems but also the implementation of the basic strategy of governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law, entrusted by the Party and the people. To accomplish the glorious mission entrusted to us by the Party and the people, we should adhere to a dialectical materialist viewpoint, be brave in exploration, and boldly practice. The Outline requires that People's Courts at all levels should focus on the following aspects to ensure the smooth progress of the reform of the People's Courts.

The leadership teams of People's Courts at all levels must earnestly strengthen leadership over reform work. Doing a good job in organization, leadership, and coordination is an important guarantee for achieving the goals of the reform of the People's Courts. In implementing the Outline, People's Courts at all levels must strengthen leadership, list reform work as an important agenda item of the Party group, with the president directly responsible, and grasp it firmly and effectively. Each Higher People's Court should establish a reform leadership group responsible for coordinating and guiding the reform work of the courts in its region. Based on the key points of the recent reform work of the People's Courts and starting from the actual local conditions, plans for the reform work of the courts in the region should be formulated. When determining specific reform steps and plans, leaders should extensively listen to the opinions of cadres and relevant parties, adhere to proceeding from the masses to the masses, open up channels for opinions, and follow good advice. At the same time, significant issues encountered during the reform process should be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court. To strengthen unified leadership, in the future, any reform measures not determined in the Outline, if local People's Courts intend to implement them, even as pilots, must be approved in advance by the Higher People's Court. Major reform measures or those likely to have a significant impact within a certain scope should be reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

We must consciously accept the leadership of local Party committees and the supervision of people's congresses at all levels. Party leadership and people's congress supervision are important guarantees for the People's Courts to perform various tasks well and ensure judicial justice. This is especially true for reform work. When implementing the tasks stipulated in the Outline, local People's Courts must consciously and proactively accept the leadership of local Party committees and the supervision of people's congresses, so as to ensure that the reform of the People's Courts advances smoothly along the correct track. When formulating reform plans and measures and implementing reform schemes, People's Courts at all levels shall promptly report to Party committees and people's congresses. Efforts shall be made to include court reform in the work agenda of Party committees and seek support from Party committees, people's congresses, and governments. Major issues and difficulties encountered during the reform shall be promptly reported to Party committees for resolution. Reports shall be made to people's congresses at appropriate times to facilitate their understanding of the progress of court reform. On issues involving matters subject to statutory appointment and removal, proactive explanations and clarifications shall be provided to people's congresses to seek support.

Cooperation from relevant departments shall be sought. The reform of the People's Courts has a strong interconnected nature; many reform measures cannot be implemented without the cooperation and coordination of relevant departments. To ensure the realization of reform objectives, People's Courts at all levels shall handle their relationships with relevant departments properly. When work involves departments such as public security, procuratorial, and judicial administrative organs, timely communication shall be made, and coordination work shall be proactively undertaken. Opinions shall be listened to with an open mind, and issues encountered during the reform shall be jointly studied and resolved through consultation. In case of major disagreements, the matter shall be promptly reported to Party committees and people's congresses for resolution.

Publicity and public opinion work concerning the reform shall be done well. The reform of the People's Courts concerns the interests of various sectors of society and the development of the national judicial system. Therefore, the necessity and importance of the reform of the People's Courts shall be publicized to the public through news media, and successful experiences and positive achievements of the reform shall be publicized, in order to gain understanding and support from all sectors of society. The Supreme People's Court shall closely cooperate with news organizations to carry out planned and prepared publicity work for reform measures that are in line with the reform direction and have achieved results, and to provide correct guidance for public opinion. For attempts that have not been tested in practice and whose success is not yet certain, they shall not be hastily reported in the media, nor shall false propaganda be made to create a sensational effect. For erroneous practices that violate legal provisions, they shall not be publicized under the guise of reform and must be resolutely corrected.

Deep-seated reform issues of the People's Courts shall be actively explored. The reforms stipulated in the Outline are the main short-term goals. We should recognize that the reform of the People's Courts is a long-term task and a difficult and complex systematic project. While completing the reform tasks stipulated in the Outline, in-depth theoretical research shall also be conducted on some major and deep-seated reform issues, and organized exploration shall be carried out. When a proposal matures, it shall be reported to the Central Committee and relevant competent authorities for approval before implementation. The main topics for reform in this regard include: proceeding from the requirements of maintaining the unity of the national legal system and achieving judicial justice, exploring the reform of the organizational system of the People's Courts; the reform of the management system for court cadres and judges; the reform of the court funding management system, and so on. The Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress has already included the amendment of the Organic Law of the People's Courts in its legislative plan. We are organizing dedicated teams to strengthen investigation and research, extensively solicit opinions, and resolve issues such as the reform of the court system through the amendment of the Organic Law of the People's Courts, and make recommendations to the Central Committee and the National People's Congress when conditions are ripe.
